SK2070 The Serilog message template has a different number of holes than the call supplies values

A Serilog logging call's constant message template declares a number of holes that is not the number of values the call passes.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitywarning
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixno
Language version floor—
Since2.0
ReSharperStructuredMessageTemplateProblem (resharper_structured_message_template_problem_highlighting)

Why

The rendered event is wrong in both directions and neither direction throws. A hole with no value is emitted as the literal text {OrderId}, so the field a dashboard queries is never populated and the message reads as a bug report about itself; a value with no hole is attached under a fabricated positional key nobody queries, so the data is present, unfindable and paid for. ⚠ The rule is deliberately Serilog-only. CA2017 already covers Microsoft.Extensions.Logging — measured against LoggerExtensions, ILogger.BeginScope and LoggerMessage.Define, handling {{ escapes, {X,10:N2} alignment and declining a non-implicit params array — and unlike CA2241, CA2253 and CA2254 it is on by default, with no AnalysisMode required. ADR-008 hosts CA* rather than rebuilding them, so what Skala implements is the half with no host at all. Serilog is where the concept is unowned, and it is also where the shape is commonest, because Serilog's own API encourages templates far richer than ILogger's.

Example

Instead of:

logger.Information("Loaded {Count} of {Total}", count);

Write:

logger.Information("Loaded {Count} of {Total}", count, total);

When it does not fire

⚠ `resharperId` is `StructuredMessageTemplateProblem`, and it was measured rather than reasoned about. It used to be null, on the argument that ReSharper dumps one issue type for the whole structured-logging family and Testing/parity-analysis/catalogued.json already credited that id to SK2016. Both halves were wrong. A probe built outside this repository against the real Serilog and Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.Abstractions packages and inspected with jb inspectcode 2025.2.6 reports `StructuredMessageTemplateProblem` on exactly this rule's finding and on nothing else: Non-existing argument in message template for a template with more holes than values, and Argument is not used in message template for more values than holes, on Serilog and on Microsoft.Extensions.Logging alike. ⚠ It did not fire on `SK2016`'s shape at all — an interpolated message produced only CSharpWarnings::CA2254, which is jb surfacing Roslyn rather than a ReSharper inspection — so the old credit pointed the id at a rule whose finding ReSharper does not report under it. SK2016 keeps TemplateIsNotCompileTimeConstantProblem, which is its concept. ⚠ `TemplateFormatStringProblem`, the id issue #20 proposes for this rule, is not the arity inspection and is not an inspection id at all — it is the id shape of the real export key resharper_template_format_string_problem_highlighting, one of the 81 rows whose id the issue-type dump does not carry, and it reported nothing on any shape in the probe. The run's canaries (ConvertIfStatementToNullCoalescingAssignment, ConvertToUsingDeclaration, RedundantUsingDirective) all fired, so the silence is the inspection's and not the harness's. ⚠ Arity is counted in holes, not in distinct names. "{X} then {X}" with two arguments is correct — Serilog binds values to holes in order — and reporting it here would be a false positive on exactly the shape SK2071 exists to describe properly. ⚠ A positional template withdraws the analysis entirely. "{0} {1}" is Serilog's string.Format mode, where arity is max-index-plus-one rather than a count, and a template mixing indices with names has semantics no rule should guess at; CA2253 is the rule that says not to write one. ⚠ A `params` array the call did not synthesise withdraws the count: logger.Information(template, args) passes an array whose length is not visible here, and counting the array itself as one value would report every such call as a mismatch. Roslyn marks the array it synthesises for a genuine params expansion as implicit, which is the only signal that separates the two. ⚠ The values are counted by parameter ordinal, never by filtering out arguments whose type does not look like a value: a reduced extension-method invocation carries its own this ILogger receiver as Arguments[0] with a real parameter symbol, and a type-name filter counts the logger as a supplied value and reports every correct call as one argument too many. Everything that is not a value — the receiver, the Exception, the LogEventLevel — precedes the template in every one of these signatures, so "after the template" is a definition rather than a heuristic. A non-constant template is not analysed, because there is no template to count; CA2254 is the rule for that. Binding is by containing type (Serilog.ILogger, Serilog.Log) and by the parameter Serilog names messageTemplate, never by method name, so a domain method called Information is not a logging call. Generated code is excluded.
